summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, a history of pancreas and kidney transplants, and a mechanical heart valve was readmitted for treatment of left foot ulcers and a significant blockage in the left superficial femoral artery. She underwent vein mapping, which showed a patent greater saphenous vein, but during surgery, it was found to be tied off, likely from a prior CABG. As a result, she had a left femoral endarterectomy with patch angioplasty instead of a bypass. She was managed postoperatively in the VICU, transitioned from heparin to Coumadin, and maintained on her home immunosuppressive and dialysis regimen. Cultures from her foot ulcer grew coagulase-negative staph, but no treatment change was needed. She worked with physical therapy, was deemed safe for discharge home with home health services, and was given detailed wound care and activity instructions. Her INR was therapeutic at discharge, and she was scheduled for follow-up in two weeks.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with ulceration
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Ulcer of other part of foot
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Heart valve replaced by other means
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
